findings: The workspace pins TypeScript at two versions: packages/registry declares ~6.0.3 (what registry sources typecheck with), root package.json declares 7.0.2 (what root tsconfig uses). The proofs resolved 6.0.3 from packages/registry/node_modules/.bin/tsc since that's the compiler the shipped mapper compiles with.

The ambient boundary packages/registry/types/rnr-boundary.d.ts:425-430 still declares the trio as required-but-nullable (fileName: string | null, not optional); this is correct (the widened production parameter accepts it) but means the codebase has two ImagePickerAsset-shaped type definitions — the production superset and the boundary subset.

The real Expo 57 SDK's mimeType field is typed `mimeType?: string` (not `?: string | null`), while fileName and fileSize are `?: string | null` and `?: number` — slight nullability inconsistency within the SDK itself; the mapper accepts all three as optional-nullable.

The registry:build script at packages/registry/scripts/build-registry.ts:140-173 fans out to both engines in a single invocation and the fan-out is deterministic (no per-engine side effects, no timestamps), which is why the freshness gate can byte-compare the emitted JSON against a fresh in-memory build.

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in a fresh worktree takes ~8s; each vitest test with real SDK compilation takes ~1-2s (tsc subprocess + scratch workspace materialization), so RED→GREEN→evidence capture is ~10-15s total.
